ADM.why: Article discusses dividend stocks and retirement income strategies but contains no information about ADM specifically, credit spreads, or FY2026 EPS guidance. No relevance to thesis or exit conditions.

ALL.why: Multiple analyst notes show price target raises (UBS $283, Morgan Stanley $260, KBW $241) and Q3 earnings beat commentary supporting the improving underwriting thesis. No catastrophe losses exceeding $2.5B mentioned. This reinforces rather than challenges the position.

APA.why: Article reports APA raising 2026 FCF forecast to $2.9B and mentions oil futures trading around $86-91/bbl, well above the $55 exit threshold. EIA commentary sees Brent near $100 for rest of year. Supports reflation thesis; no exit signal.

DLTR.why: Articles mention DLTR competing with traditional retailers and reference retail sector breakouts, but contain no specific Q3 EPS guidance cuts or information below the $0.80 threshold. No direct threat to thesis.

DXCM.why: Articles reference conference presentation and competitive landscape but provide no guidance cuts on operating margins below 20% or disclosure of refinancing difficulties related to October 2026 credit facility maturity. No exit signal triggered.

KMX.why: Article titled 'Can Carvana Stock Fall 40%?' raises bearish sentiment on the used-car retail sector. While not specific to KMX's unit margin guidance, it signals broader sector weakness that could pressure KMX margins. Monitor for evidence of margin deterioration exceeding $200/unit guidance.

LPG.why: Energy shippers report on tanker market tightness and oil futures trading higher (~$88-94/bbl). Supports strength in VLGC freight rates. No indication of Q2 2027 revenue falling below $120M.

MU.why: Multiple articles report strong AI infrastructure demand, memory stock rallies, and positive earnings revisions. CoreWeave CEO states AI demand outpaces capacity. No evidence of gross-margin guidance cut below 80%. Reinforces contractual margin protection thesis.

PBF.why: Articles highlight tight refined product supplies, strong refining margins, and PBF's competitive positioning. Oil prices stable near $88-94/bbl, well above $70 exit threshold. News reinforces macro tailwind thesis.

RS.why: Exit condition references October 21 Q3 earnings release testing year-over-year Metals Service Centers revenue decline. Article discusses STLD buyback and steel sector dynamics but does not report RS earnings or revenue data. Awaiting the specified earnings report.

SEI.why: Needham maintains Buy and raises price target from $104 to $126, supporting the positive revision thesis. However, article does not address customer concentration risk (63% of revenue from single customer) or cash burn concerns. Price target raise is supportive but lacks visibility into key risks.

VCTR.why: Article reports October 2026 total client assets and notes stock rocketing 104% after earnings, confirming continued positive momentum. No evidence of net client outflows reversing the $4.1B net inflows from June quarter.
